subject: Acceptance cushion and escalation corridor
messages:
From: Emily Chen <e.chen@helioshealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Dan Patel <d.patel@heliosprocure.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP v3 + procurement timing risk

Hi Vanessa / Camila,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — team is excited about the latency and routing features. Attached is the updated MAP (HL-4821-MAP-v3.pdf) with the evaluation gate dates filled in. Two items to flag from procurement:

- Procurement at Helios needs signed IP and data isolation language before purchase order; that could add ~2 weeks. Dan (cc) is the procurement lead.
- Our internal security review wants more detail on KMS integration; they'll finish by 6/21 but that date is soft.

Given those levers, we'd like to propose a modest acceptance cushion so our go-live stays aligned with internal QA. Can Redwood confirm whether a short two-week shift to the acceptance window is workable without impacting the dedicated capacity commit?

I attached a simple timeline (Procurement-timeline-note.xlsx) and highlighted where Helios expects risk. Happy to discuss on a quick sync.

Thanks,
Emily Chen
Director, Platform Integrations
Helios Health

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <e.chen@helioshealth.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP v3 + procurement timing risk

Emily — thanks for the note and the concise timeline. I reviewed the MAP and the procurement spreadsheet. Short answers up front: we can accommodate a two-week acceptance cushion, but there are three items to reconcile before I commit to a formal rebaseline:

1) Dedicated capacity reservation: shifting acceptance by two weeks overlaps with another committed burst in the week of 6/28. Marcus, can you confirm whether we can hold the reserved pool and still guarantee the throughput SLOs for HL-4821?

2) SLA exception: we can draft a temporary SLA exception if needed, but that requires a formal sign-off. Please send any internal sign-off template Helios uses for approvals so legal can mirror it.

3) KMS/Key management detail: our private deployment playbook needs the exact KMS provider + key lifecycle expectations. Camila — can you earmark the integration spec and notify security of the proposed timeline?

If Helios can commit to the purchase order clearance by 6/21 (or provide a concrete blocker list by 6/15), we can do the two-week cushion and absorb the minimal risk. Otherwise, we should prepare an escalation corridor: a short credit or a partial fallback to a hosted variant while migration finishes.

Propose 30-minute sync tomorrow 10:30am PT to align.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Sales Director, Redwood Inference
[attachment: SLA-exception-request.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Emily Chen <e.chen@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 08:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP v3 + procurement timing risk

On Tue, Jun 8, 2027 at 11:03 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
> Emily — thanks for the note and the concise timeline. I reviewed the MAP and the procurement spreadsheet. Short answers up front: we can accommodate a two-week acceptance cushion, but there are three items to reconcile before I commit to a formal rebaseline:

Emily / team — quick technical read:

- KMS: we support customer-managed KMS on Private with standard HSM-backed keys. To finalize, we need the key naming policy and whether Helios will rotate keys monthly or quarterly. If monthly, that nudges our runbook updates but is still fine.
- Capacity: Marcus — the burst on 6/28 is a short performance test for another account. If we punt that test by one week, we can avoid oversubscription. Marcus, can you advise feasibility?
- Rollback path: recommend we include a controlled fallback in the MAP: should procurement run late, we provision a temporary hosted instance for up to 14 days (no data persistence), then switch to Private once approvals are in. That keeps Helios' QA on schedule.

Risk log (high level):
- Procurement sign-off delay — impact: +10–14 days to acceptance. Mitigation: escrow the hosted fallback and assign procurement liaison.
- KMS spec gap — impact: engineering effort +3–5 days. Mitigation: template KMS spec and quick sync with Helios security.
- Payment terms / PO timing — impact: hold on deployment. Mitigation: legal SLA exception and credit buffer for delayed acceptance.

I'll attach the KMS checklist and propose the hosted fallback as an explicit MAP lane.

—Camila
Camila Reyes
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
[attachment: KMS-integration-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Emily Chen <e.chen@helioshealth.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP v3 + procurement timing risk — capacity & escalation note

Team — quick capacity call-out and recommended escalation wording.

We ran the reservation planner this morning. Confirmation: we can hold the dedicated pool for HL-4821 through the 2-week cushion if the 6/28 test is deferred by one week. Impact to other customers is minimal (5% extra run-time on the burst).

Recommended escalation corridor (to be shared with Helios execs if procurement slips):
1) Formal rebaseline: shift acceptance window by 14 days, update MAP v3 with the hosted-fallback lane, and include a one-time credit equal to 5% of first-year committed spend if PO is delayed beyond revised date.
2) Temporary hosted fallback: enable hosted instance for up to 14 days while Private completes KMS/legal gates. Data persistence is disabled; customer will test against non-persistent environment.
3) Exec escalation: if PO is not cleared within 7 days of the revised acceptance date, we escalate to the Redwood Account Director and Helios' procurement lead for an expedited decision.

I'll prepare a short note with the proposed credit language for legal. Vanessa — if you approve, I can escalate and put the revised MAP in HubSpot after your sign-off.

Marcus Lin
Infrastructure Capacity Lead, Redwood Inference
